rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life’s route to happiness is fixed by the true order disclosed in human nature and the cosmic system, which God decreed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links this to 30:30.
rows.anchor: فسنة الحياة التي تنتهي بسالكها إلى السعادة الإنسانية طريقة متعينة يقتضيها النظام بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the truth conformed to their whims, cosmic elements, causes, and regular relations would have to change into arbitrary, conflicting relations, corrupting the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: فلو اتبع الحق أهواءهم فاقتضى لهم من الشرع ما تجازف به أهواؤهم لم يكن ذلك إلا بتغير أجزاء الكون عما هي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cosmic existence and its governance are inseparable, as are creation and command; this is why changing the order would corrupt both the world and its administration.
rows.anchor: لأن كينونتها وتدبيرها مختلطان غير متمايزين، والخلق والأمر متصلان غير منفصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘reminder’ is the Qur’an, as in 21:50 and 43:44.
rows.anchor: لا ريب أن المراد بالذكر هو القرآن كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it a reminder after the charge that the Prophet was possessed counterposes their insult that the bearer of the reminder was mad (15:6).
rows.anchor: ولعل التعبير عنه بالذكر بعد قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an reminds them of God or recalls God’s religion of true belief and good works; the latter sense better fits the preceding context.
rows.anchor: لأنه يذكرهم بالله أو يذكر لهم دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is called ‘their’ religion because the true call varies in generality and detail among peoples, and this final revelation is the last stage of detailed law; they reject the religion proper to them.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضيف إليهم لأن الدين أعني الدعوة الحقة مختلفة بالنسبة إلى الناس بالإجمال والتفصيل والذي يذكره القرآن آخر مراحل التفصيل

rows.speaker: كثير منهم
rows.claim: Many commentators take the possessive ‘their reminder’ as an honorific; they compare the phrase to the Qur’an’s statement that it is a reminder for the Prophet and his people (43:44).
rows.anchor: وقال كثير منهم إن إضافة الذكر إليهم للتشريف نظير قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Qur’an honors the Prophet, his household, Arabs, and the community, ‘their’ denotes this religion’s specific relation to the community, which fits the context better.
rows.anchor: غير أن الإضافة في الآية ليست لهذه العناية بل لعناية اختصاص هذا الدين بهذه الأمة وهو الأوفق لصدر الآية

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān says kharāj and kharj share the sense of revenue or produce paid as an assigned due.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان أصل الخراج والخرج واحد وهو الغلة التي يخرج على سبيل الوظيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the fourth rejected excuse: they allege the Prophet asks them for a customary payment, but God provides for him, so he needs no revenue from them; compare 11:51.
rows.anchor: أي مالا يدفعونه إليك على سبيل الرسم والوظيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two rejected excuses concern the Qur’an and the religion’s novelty relative to earlier peoples, respectively.
rows.anchor: فأولها { أفلم يدبروا القول } راجع إلى القرآن والثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third excuse targets the Prophet himself with the claim of madness; the fourth targets his conduct by alleging that he asks for payment.
rows.anchor: والثالث { أم يقولون به جنة } إلى نفس النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، والرابع { أم تسألهم خرجا } إلى سيرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukūb means turning away from a road or veering from something.
rows.anchor: النكب والنكوب العدول عن الطريق والميل عن الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is clear, consistent in its judgment, and carries its travelers to their intended goal; this is the nature of truth.
rows.anchor: الصراط المستقيم هو الطريق الواضح الذي لا يختلف ولا يتخلف في حكمه وهو إيصاله سالكيه إلى الغاية المقصودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is one: its parts do not contradict or conflict, and it does not fail to reach the end toward which it guides.
rows.anchor: فإن الحق واحد لا يختلف أجزاؤه بالتناقض والتدافع ولا يتخلف في مطلوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet guides to truth, he necessarily guides to the straight path; those who hate truth turn away from that path.
rows.anchor: وإذ ذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يهدي إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary singles out denial of the afterlife because true religion rests on enduring life after death, where happiness must be gained through true belief and good works and misery avoided.
rows.anchor: وإنما أورد من أوصافهم عدم إيمانهم بالآخرة واقتصر عليه لأن دين الحق مبني على أساس أن للإنسان حياة خالدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious duties require accounting and recompense on Judgment Day; those who deny it see religion as futile and life as material pleasure, so desire governs them regardless of truth.
rows.anchor: والتكليف لا يتم إلا بحساب وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lack of faith in the afterlife leaves them pursuing whim whether it agrees with truth or opposes it.
rows.anchor: ولازم ذلك أن يكون المتبع عندهم الهوى وافق الحق أو خالفه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines lijāj as persistence and obstinacy in a forbidden act, and ʿamah as bewildered hesitation in a matter.
rows.anchor: والعمه التردد في الأمر من التحير، ذكرهما الراغب

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān glosses istikāna as submission, an istifʿāl form from kawn: they did not seek to be in a submissive state.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع الاستكانة الخضوع وهو استفعال من الكون

words: ولو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if God relieved their distress, they would answer with no gratitude, persist in rebellion and perplexity, and gain no benefit from mercy, just as threats do not benefit them.
rows.anchor: لو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر لم يرجعوا بمقابلة ذلك الشكر بل أصروا على تمردهم عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment was a light chastisement that did not cut them off from ordinary means, as indicated by the following verse; this avoids the objection that desperate people instinctively return to God.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعذاب العذاب الخفيف الذي لا ينقطع به الإنسان عن عامة الأسباب بقرينة ما في الآية التالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent problem is that people instinctively turn to God in distress when cut off from ordinary causes, a pattern repeated elsewhere in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: لا يرد أن الرجوع إلى الله تعالى عند الاضطرار والانقطاع عن الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community’s ifāḍa in a report means plunging into and discussing it.
rows.anchor: إفاضة القوم في الحديث خوضهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with the earlier ‘if not for God’s grace’ and constitutes a second rebuke of the believers.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { لولا إذ سمعتموه } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning grace and mercy in this world and the next indicates that the threatened severe punishment would affect both worlds.
rows.anchor: بقوله { في الدنيا والآخرة } دلالة على كون العذاب المذكور ذيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase ‘when you received it with your tongues’ modifies ‘you plunged into it.’
rows.anchor: الظرف متعلق بقوله { أفضتم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the report ‘with tongues’ depicts gossip passed from tongue to tongue without verification or reflection.
rows.anchor: وتقييد التلقي بالألسنة للدلالة على أنه كان مجرد انتقال القول من لسان إلى لسان من غير تثبت وتدبر فيه

words: وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيْسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about saying it with mouths is explanatory coordination with the preceding phrase; mouth-only speech lacked confirmation in the heart and had no reality beyond utterance.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فقوله { وتقولون بأفواهكم ما ليس لكم به علم } من قبيل عطف التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added reference to mouths stresses that the claim was unverified in the heart and existed only as speech.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى أن القول لم يكن عن تثبت وتبين قلبي

words: وَتَحْسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنًۭا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They treated uninformed gossip as trivial, but it was grave slander; because it concerned the Prophet, its circulation damaged his standing and the religious mission.
rows.anchor: وشيوع إفك هذا شأنه بين الناس يفضحه عندهم ويفسد أمر الدعوة الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Glory be to You’ is a parenthetical declaration of God’s transcendence; Qur’anic etiquette invokes glorification when declaring anyone innocent.
rows.anchor: اعتراض بالتنزيه لله سبحانه وهو من أدب القرآن أن ينزه الله بالتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buhtān means fabrication and is so named because it overwhelms and astonishes the person falsely accused.
rows.anchor: والبهتان الافتراء سمي به لأنه يبهت الإنسان المفترى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is an immense slander because it attacks honor, especially the Prophet’s, and asserts a claim without knowledge or proof, as the witness requirement in 24:13 shows.
rows.anchor: وكونه بهتانا عظيما لأنه افتراء في عرض وخاصة إذ كان متعلقا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: يعظكم الله أن تعودوا لمثله أبدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verses exhort believers never to repeat an act like this.
rows.anchor: موعظة بالنهي عن العود لمثله

words: إن الذين يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this verse belongs to the connected verses about the slander, it threatens those who spread the adultery accusation without proof, since they delight in circulating indecency among believers.
rows.anchor: إن كانت الآية نازلة في جملة آيات الإفك ومتصلة بما تقدمها وموردها الرمي بالزنا بغير بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-fāḥisha may mean indecency generally, including fornication, slander, and other obscene acts.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالفاحشة مطلق الفحشاء كالزنا والقذف وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loving the spread of indecency among believers, including slander, warrants painful punishment for its lovers in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وحب شيوعها ومنها القذف في المؤمنين يستوجب عذابا أليما لمحبيه في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a possible reading, the definite noun refers specifically to the accusation, and ‘loving its spread’ figuratively means actually circulating it; the worldly punishment could then be the legal hadd.
rows.anchor: لو كان اللام في { الفاحشة } للعهد والمراد بها القذف وكان حب الشيوع كناية عن قصه الشيوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that reading: context does not support it, and the hadd follows from one accusation without requiring an intent to spread it.
rows.anchor: على أن الرمي بمجرد تحققه مرة موجب للحد ولا موجب لتقييده بقصد الشيوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement emphasizes the gravity of God’s anger over the matter, even where people fail to recognize it.
rows.anchor: تأكيد وإعظام لما فيه من سخط الله وغضبه وإن جهله الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mention of grace and mercy renews the reminder of God’s favor.
rows.anchor: تكرارا للامتنان ومعناه ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his commentary on the parallel command in 2:208.
rows.anchor: تقدم تفسير الآية في الآية 208 من سورة البقرة في الجزء الثاني من الكتاب

words: وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated appeal to grace, now explicitly answered by ‘none would be purified,’ reflects that God alone bestows goodness and salvation; the Qur’an says good is in His hand and good that reaches people is from Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما يدل عليه العقل فإن مفيض الخير والسعادة هو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills to purify those prepared for purification who ask for it through their state of readiness; He hears their request and knows their preparedness.
rows.anchor: ولا يشاء إلا تزكية من استعد لها وسأله بلسان استعداده ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is hearing of the request for purification and knowing of the person’s readiness for it.
rows.anchor: أي سميع لسؤال من سأله التزكية عليم بحال من استعد لها

words: وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʾtilāʾ can mean falling short, abandoning, or swearing; all three senses fit the instruction to continue aid.
rows.anchor: الايتلاء التقصير والترك والحلف، وكل من المعاني الثلاثة لا يخلو من مناسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy should not fall short in giving to relatives, poor people, and emigrants, abandon them, or swear to stop giving.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا يقصر أولو الفضل منكم والسعة يعني الأغنياء في إيتاء أولي القرابة والمساكين والمهاجرين في سبيل الله من مالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God urges forgiveness and forbearance by asking whether they would not love God to forgive them.
rows.anchor: ثم حرضهم بقوله { ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this verse is part of the slander passage, some believers had resolved to cut off aid they had been giving to certain participants in the slander; God forbids that and urges continued giving.
rows.anchor: على تقدير نزولها في جملة الآيات واتصالها بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Light upon light’ is the predicate of an omitted subject, a pronoun referring from context to the light of the glass.
rows.anchor: وقوله { نور على نور } خبر لمبتدأ محذوف وهو ضمير راجع إلى نور الزجاجة المفهوم من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glass’s light is an immense light upon light, expressing perfect brightness.
rows.anchor: والمعنى نور الزجاجة المذكور نور عظيم على نور كذلك أي في كمال التلمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the phrase as intensified light without counting separate lights: it means unbounded doubling, not one specified or unspecified light above another, nor exactly two lights; the author finds this sound.
rows.anchor: قيل هو تضاعف النور لا تعدده فليس المراد به أنه نور معين أو غير معين فوق نور آخر مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī also sees a subtle dual relation: light genuinely comes from the lamp and figuratively from the glass, yielding two relations though the lamp is the true source.
rows.anchor: فإن للنور الشارق من المصباح نسبة إليه بالأصالة والحقيقة ونسبة إلى الزجاجة التي عليه بالاستعارة والمجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, faith and knowledge shine as borrowed light in believers’ hearts, taken from God’s light and dependent on it.
rows.anchor: فإن نور الإيمان والمعرفة نور مستعار مشرق على قلوب المؤمنين مقتبس من نوره تعالى قائم به مستمد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The represented reality is God’s light shining in believers’ hearts; its simile is light from a glass-covered lamp with pure oil set in a niche.
rows.anchor: فقد تحصل أن الممثل له هو نور الله المشرق على قلوب المؤمنين والمثل هو المشبه به النور المشرق من زجاجة على مصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The niche gathers the light and reflects it outward into the room, making it shine with exceptional force and quality.
rows.anchor: فإن نور المصباح المشرق من الزجاجة والمشكاة تجمعه وتعكسه على المستنيرين به يشرق عليهم في نهاية القوة والجودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive tree’s neither-east-nor-west position signifies pure, fine oil, while the oil nearly glowing without fire signals the quality and clarity of the emitted light.
rows.anchor: واعتبار كون الدهن من شجرة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية للدلالة على صفاء الدهن وجودته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, ‘whomever He wills’ refers to the men described next as fully faithful, including those not distracted from God’s remembrance by trade or sale.
rows.anchor: فمن المعلوم من السياق أن المراد بقوله { من يشاء } القوم الذين ذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not mean God arbitrarily selects some individuals and then requires a separate appeal to their receptivity; the context identifies the guided with people of complete faith.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى أن الله يهدي بعض الأفراد إلى نوره دون بعض بمشيئة ذلك حتى يحتاج في تتميمه إلى القول بأنه إنما يشاء الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites Qur’anic uses of ‘the worlds’ in statements of preference or distinction, at 3:42 and 45:16.
rows.anchor: واصطفاك على نساء العالمين آل عمران 42 وقوله وفضلناهم على العالمين الجاثية 16

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nadhīr means munthir, ‘one who warns,’ as some say; warning is close in meaning to frightening.
rows.anchor: والنذير بمعنى المنذر على ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabāraka means abundant good is established in the one who sent the Furqān down to Muhammad, His servant; that good flows from God to creation through revelation.
rows.anchor: أي ثبت وتحقق خير كثير فيمن نزل الفرقان على عبده محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Furqān is a book that distinguishes truth from falsehood, rescues the worlds from error, and directs them to guidance.
rows.anchor: حيث نزل على عبده كتابا فارقا بين الحق والباطل منقذا للعالمين من الضلال سائقا لهم إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of God’s revelation, the Prophet as His commissioned servant and warner, and the Qur’an as Furqān prepares the answer to pagan claims that the Qur’an was fabricated and the Prophet was merely an ordinary man.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك تمهيد لما سيحكي - عن المشركين من طعنهم في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s overwhelming proof distinguishes truth from falsehood, so it is true; the obedient servant calls to truth, and God’s miraculous speech attests to his mission.
rows.anchor: فالمحصل أنه كتاب يفرق بحجته الباهرة بين الحق والباطل فلا يكون إلا حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret Furqān as all revealed scriptures and ‘His servant’ as all prophets; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as far from the wording’s apparent sense.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر ما في قول بعضهم إن المراد بالفرقان مطلق الكتب السماوية المنزلة على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is purposive: the goal of revelation to the Prophet is that he warn all the worlds, meaning all humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: اللام للتعليل وتدل على أن غاية تنزيل الفرقان على عبده أن يكون منذرا لجميع العالمين من الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural denotes universal scope; its plural form may also suggest that all people share one God, unlike pagan groups with different deities.
rows.anchor: والجمع المحلى باللام يفيد الاستغراق، ولا يخلو الإتيان بصيغة الجمع المحلى باللام من إشارة إلى أن للجميع إلها واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse mentions warning rather than good news because the sūra’s discourse is framed as warning and threat.
rows.anchor: والاكتفاء بذكر الإنذار دون التبشير لأن الكلام في السورة مسوق سوق الإنذار والتخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mulk/al-milk describes something’s dependence on another that may dispose of it as it wills, whether by ownership of its substance or by sovereign command and rule.
rows.anchor: الملك بكسر الميم وفتحها قيام شيء بشيء بحيث يتصرف فيه كيف شاء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes mulk, rule by command and prohibition over a people, from milk, control of what is possessed; the latter is broader, and every mulk is milk but not vice versa.
rows.anchor: كما قال الراغب الملك - بفتح الميم وكسر اللام - هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says mulk is control of an object subject to judgment, while milk is the wider genus; some reserve milk for ownership of the substance and mulk for other rule.
rows.anchor: فالملك بالضم - ضبط الشيء المتصرف فيه بالحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of exclusive possession means the heavens and earth are not self-sufficient in any respect; God alone rules and administers them absolutely.
rows.anchor: واللام للاختصاص - يفيد أن السماوات والأرض مملوكة له غير مستقلة بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An owner may take a child to help manage limited affairs or to inherit after death; God has power over everything and eternal dominion, so He needs no child, refuting pagans and Christians.
rows.anchor: فإن الملك على الإطلاق لا يدع حاجة إلى اتخاذ الولد إذ اتخاذ الولد لأحد أمرين

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A partner is needed only when one’s rule does not cover everything; God’s dominion encompasses every thing and aspect, refuting polytheists.
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى بعده { ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } فإن الحاجة إلى الشريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and determination show that all affairs return to God alone: things arise through prior and concurrent causes, which determine their existence and effects within the observed order.
rows.anchor: أن الخلقة لما كانت بتوسيط الأسباب المتقدمة على الشيء والمقارنة له استلزم ذلك ارتباط وجودات الأشياء بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone creates, He alone determines and governs; absolute ownership entails creation, creation entails determination, and determination entails administration, establishing His sole lordship.
rows.anchor: وقيام الخلقة به يستلزم قيام التقدير به، لكون التقدير متفرعا على الخلقة

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: الوثنيون
rows.claim: Although they acknowledged God’s universal ownership, polytheists held that He delegated partial sovereignty and lordship to their gods, making each a lesser lord beneath the Lord of lords.
rows.anchor: كان الوثنيون مع تسليمهم عموم ملكه يرون أن ملكه للجميع وربوبيته للكل لا ينافي ملك آلهتهم وربوبيتهم للبعض بتفويضه تعالى ذلك إليهم

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ
rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The polytheists’ pilgrimage formula allowed an exception: a partner belonged to God, who owned that partner and what it owned.
rows.anchor: فقد كانوا يقولون في تلبية الحج لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal ownership alone does not disprove their delegated gods, because they could imagine God retaining ownership while assigning some affairs to created partners.
rows.anchor: فلذلك لم يكف قوله { الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض } لإثبات اختصاص الربوبية به تعالى قبالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and determination necessarily entail governance, so God manages every thing and has delegated no affairs to another.
rows.anchor: فاجيب عنه بأن الخلق له سبحانه والتقدير يلازمه وإذا اجتمعا لزمهما التدبير فله سبحانه تدبير كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first establishes absolute ownership to deny a child or partner, then explains that ownership through universal creation and determination, which entails God’s direct rule.
rows.anchor: فقد تحصل أن قوله { الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } مسوق لتوحيد الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī omits other interpretations of this and the preceding verse because he sees no useful point in them.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية والتي قبلها لهم أقوال أخر أغمضنا عن إيرادها لخلوها عن الجدوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists’ idols are neither creators nor owners of anything; they are manufactured objects, so they lack the attributes proper to a deity.
rows.anchor: أصناما ليست بخالقة شيئا بل هي مخلوقة مصنوعة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unintroduced pronoun in ‘they took’ refers from context to the polytheists; this phrasing conveys contempt and disparagement.
rows.anchor: وضمير { واتخذوا } للمشركين على ما يفيده السياق وإن لم يسبق لهم ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols gods and immediately saying they create nothing but are themselves created shows that divinity is only a name assigned to them, without its reality.
rows.anchor: وتوصيفها بالآلهة مع تعقيبها بمثل قوله { لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون } إشارة إلى أن ليس لها من الألوهية إلا اسم سموها به
